title: Shadow telemetry discovery and visibility restoration for Console
creator: Amaya Chen
description:
Summary: During a capacity event on 2026-02-18 we observed several console pages showing stale or empty graphs while downstream inference remained healthy. Investigation found multiple "shadow" telemetry gaps: (1) a sampling policy that dropped low-frequency error traces from long-tail tenants, (2) aggregated dashboards that hid per-tenant queue pressure, and (3) missing instrumentation on the async retry path used by the ingress proxy. These blind spots delayed the on-call team’s ability to identify the root cause (a tenant-specific KV-cache eviction storm combined with an autoscale policy mismatch).

Goal: Restore end-to-end visibility for the console surface so a single on-call runbook can identify tenant-level saturation, cross-service retry storms, and KV-cache churn within 10 minutes of an incident. Work focuses on adding targeted metrics, reworking dashboard aggregation, and filling tracepoints along the retry/eviction path.

What we learned:
- Sampling rules: Current head-sampling prioritized high-throughput customers and dropped low-volume long-tail tenants. That masked a tenant-specific error mode.
- Aggregation smoothing: Several console dashboards show p50/p95 only; they were averaged across shards which flattened spike signals.
- Missing spans: The ingress async retrier and the KV eviction pathway lacked span IDs and correlation keys, making causal tracing impossible.
- Retrospective trade-offs: We intentionally removed some high-cardinality metrics to save ingestion cost; the incident shows we need selective reintroduction with controlled retention.

Success criteria:
- Per-tenant queue_depth and kv_eviction_count visible in the console and alertable within 5 minutes of a spike.
- A new tracepoint on ingress retrier + eviction path with tenant correlation ID preserved end-to-end.
- Dashboards show both aggregated rollups and a heatmap view for the 99th percentile tail across tenants.

Risks and mitigation:
- Cost: Adding per-tenant metrics increases ingestion; we will limit retention to 7 days for high-cardinality metrics and use sampling windows.
- Noise: New alerts could be noisy; we'll add a probation period and tune thresholds using incident replay data.

Stakeholders: Console SREs, Runtime Reliability, Product (Console UX), Applied ML (for KV behavior context).
